name: Payback Period
description: Calculate the payback period as investment cost over annual cash flow.
formula: Payback Period = Investment Cost / Annual Cash Flow
business_contexts: a manufacturer assessing payback period on a new equipment purchase
a retailer assessing payback period on a store buildout
a software company assessing payback period on a platform investment
a utility assessing payback period on an infrastructure upgrade
a restaurant assessing payback period on a renovation
question_patterns: Given the investment cost and annual cash flow below, what is the payback period?
Calculate the payback period from the figures given.
How many years until the investment pays back, given the figures below?
Calculate payback period by dividing investment cost by annual cash flow given.
Using the figures below, what is the payback period, in years?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate payback period = investment_cost / annual_cash_flow
key_insight: Payback period only measures how long it takes to recover the investment — it says nothing about profitability afterward, which is why it's paired with ROI or NPV in a real evaluation.
common_mistakes: Dividing annual cash flow by investment cost instead of the other way around
Treating a short payback period alone as proof the investment is worthwhile, ignoring returns beyond the payback point
framework_soundbite: Payback period is investment over annual cash flow — how long until you get your money back, nothing about what happens after.
